overall: Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes; AG declined to review the Chair's authority to revise minutes and the non-OML and unfiled allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair lacked authority to revise the clerk's draft of the August 5 minutes and stripped her language, inserting his own.
allegations.key_passage: An allegation that the Chair “stripped away” the Complainant’s language from the minutes and replaced it with his own, even if true, does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law; therefore, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair's revisions made the August 5 minutes inaccurate or insufficiently detailed in violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we do not find that the version of the minutes that the Board ultimately approved was insufficient, and we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised harassment, sexism, misogyny, gender discrimination, and unprofessionalism concerns, plus the Board's review of the complaint, not all in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: allegations regarding harassment, unprofessionalism, and incivility do not allege violations of the Open Meeting Law; as such, we decline to review these allegations.

allegations.summary: Several allegations raised in later communications were not in the original complaint filed with the Board, so the AG did not review them.
allegations.key_passage: First, we do not review allegations that were not raised in an Open Meeting Law complaint filed with the public body.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
